impact: The T-010 re-spec draft must rewrite criterion 1 to: (a) name the manifest renameSync as the commit boundary explicitly; (b) require every failure strictly BEFORE the rename — generation write/fsync, manifest temp write/fsync, and the rename itself (real errnos: ENOENT/EXDEV/EACCES, provoked not just injected) — to preserve the prior manifest, served intact afterward; (c) require any failure AFTER the rename (parent-directory fsync, candidate cleanup) to return committed-with-warning — never reported as a failed publish, never thrown — with both referenced generations retained; (d) require crash recovery to accept EITHER complete, checksum-valid manifest after a simulated crash at any boundary, never to demand restoring the pre-rename one; (e) encode the structural nothing-after-commit-may-throw rule: every hook/cleanup callable is read into a local before the commit step (the findings' three-review-round lesson — fix the rule, not the statement); (f) coordinate with ISS-030's durability decision: if the recorded no-fsync-for-snapshots policy is adopted, the 'ENOSPC during each of the fsyncs' clauses reduce to coordination-state fsyncs and criterion 1 must be reworded off the five-step fsync ladder entirely rather than left contradicting the settled policy.
resolution: Fixed by the v0.2/v0.3 ticket re-spec applied 2026-08-02: T-010 acceptance criterion 1 now demands rename-boundary process-crash atomicity proven by failure injection — not the impossible post-rename recovery guarantee — and states the power-loss honesty explicitly. The full verified requirements record is preserved in this issue's impact field.
title: T-010 acceptance criterion 1 requires a post-rename recovery guarantee that cannot be implemented
